raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-style Anthropic clients (for example DeepSeek Harness) call `/v1/messages` with `thinking={"type": "enabled"}` and no `budget_tokens`; they carry the reasoning strength in `output_config.effort` instead. `AnthropicThinkingParam` rejects these requests with a 400 (`thinking.budget_tokens is required when thinking.type is 'enabled'`), so these clients cannot use a DeepSeek-V4.1 SGLang server at all.

The budget has no effect here: the local backend has no hard-cap knob, and `serving.py` only logs it as "not enforced". Requiring it only breaks clients and gives them nothing in return. We ran DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash behind such a client by patching this check locally, and this PR moves that fix upstream.

## Modifications

- `anthropic/protocol.py`: `budget_tokens` is optional on `type="enabled"`. When it is given, it must still be `>= 1024`. The `disabled` and `adaptive` rules are unchanged. The docstring now records the deviation from the SDK and the reason for it.
- `anthropic/serving.py`: the comment describing the protocol shape is updated to match.
- `test_serving.py`: `test_request_thinking_enabled_requires_budget_tokens` is replaced by `test_request_thinking_enabled_without_budget_tokens_is_accepted`. The new test asserts that the request parses, reasoning is enabled, and no unenforced-budget warning is logged. The existing `< 1024` rejection test and the "with budget, logs warning" test still pass unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: request validation only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Lines stay within the existing style. Pre-commit was not run locally.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py`: 68 passed.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Docstring updated.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. Not applicable.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Hi maintainers, this PR is from an external contributor, so I can't add the `run-ci` label myself, and the `pr-gate` checks are failing only because the label is missing.

Locally, `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, and the registered-test checks), and `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py` passes (68 tests).

Could someone add `run-ci` to trigger CI? Thanks!

Hi @JustinTong0323, gentle ping on this one when you have a moment.

Current `main` still rejects `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}` without `budget_tokens` (the validator in `entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py`), so clients that send `enabled` without a budget get a 400. This PR relaxes only that check; the 68 tests in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py` pass locally.

The `pr-gate` failures are only the missing `run-ci` label, which I can't add as an external contributor. Could you add `run-ci` and take a look? Happy to rebase onto the latest `main` or adjust anything. Thanks!

CI status note: the recurring red on `base-b-test-1-gpu-large (1)` is the deterministic main-wide failure tracked in #45846 (`test_basic_sanity_dspark` logprob mismatch, bit-identical across PRs/reruns) — unrelated to this change. The anthropic unit tests and all other shards are green on every attempt. Will update-branch and rerun once #45846 is fixed on main.

Change itself is sound — the budget is unenforced either way, so requiring it bought nothing. Flagging the intentional Anthropic-API deviation inline so it lands as a conscious merge decision rather than by accident.

Marking this explicitly: relaxing the required `budget_tokens` deviates from the Anthropic API contract — the real Messages API 400s on `thinking.type=enabled` without it, and `budget_tokens` is a required field in the SDK's `ThinkingConfigEnabled`, so official-SDK clients can't even construct the request this PR now accepts. It's an accept-superset relaxation aimed at non-SDK clients, consistent with this endpoint's accept-and-log stance (the budget is unenforced even when provided), so I think it's the right call — but if we ever move toward strict API mirroring, or later implement a real budget hard-cap, this relaxation needs to be revisited.

     union of three variants — see ``anthropic-sdk-python``'s
     ``thinking_config_{enabled,disabled,adaptive}_param.py``:
 
-    * ``enabled`` requires ``budget_tokens`` (≥1024) and accepts
-      ``display``.
+    * ``enabled`` accepts ``budget_tokens`` (≥1024 when given) and
+      ``display``. The SDK requires ``budget_tokens`` here, but the local
+      backend never uses it, so it is optional: DeepSeek-style clients send
+      ``{"type": "enabled"}`` and carry the strength in
+      ``output_config.effort``.
     * ``disabled`` accepts no other fields.
     * ``adaptive`` (Claude 4.7) accepts ``display`` but not
       ``budget_tokens``.

     def _validate_thinking_shape(self):
         # Cross-field rules mirror the SDK's three discriminated variants.
         if self.type == "enabled":
-            if self.budget_tokens is None:
-                raise ValueError(
-                    "thinking.budget_tokens is required when thinking.type is 'enabled'"
-                )
-            if self.budget_tokens < 1024:
+            # Deliberate deviation from the Anthropic API, which rejects
+            # type="enabled" without budget_tokens (see class docstring).
+            if self.budget_tokens is not None and self.budget_tokens < 1024:
                 raise ValueError(
                     "thinking.budget_tokens must be >= 1024 (got {})".format(
                         self.budget_tokens

@@ -578,8 +578,8 @@ def _emit_user_message(parts: list[dict]) -> None:

         if anthropic_request.thinking is not None:

+            # The protocol layer already enforces the thinking shape:
+            #   enabled  -> budget_tokens optional (>=1024 if given), display optional
             #   disabled -> neither budget_tokens nor display allowed

             # So by the time we get here ``budget_tokens`` can only be

             f"expected unenforced-budget warning: {log.output}",
         )
 
-    def test_request_thinking_enabled_requires_budget_tokens(self):
-        """SDK requires ``budget_tokens`` for ``type=enabled`` — Pydantic 400."""
-        from pydantic import ValidationError
-
-        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError) as ctx:
-            self._anthropic_request(thinking={"type": "enabled"}, stream=False)
-        self.assertIn("budget_tokens", str(ctx.exception))
+    def test_request_thinking_enabled_without_budget_tokens_is_accepted(self):
+        """DeepSeek-style clients send ``{"type": "enabled"}`` without
+        ``budget_tokens``. The backend never uses the budget, so the request
+        is accepted, reasoning is enabled, and no unenforced-budget warning

+        serving = self._serving()
+        request = self._anthropic_request(thinking={"type": "enabled"}, stream=False)
+        self.assertIsNone(request.thinking.budget_tokens)
+        with self.assertNoLogs(
+            "sglang.srt.entrypoints.anthropic.serving", level="WARNING"
+        ):
+            serving._convert_to_chat_completion_request(request)
+        self.assertEqual(serving.openai_serving_chat.apply_reasoning_calls, [True])
 
     def test_request_thinking_enabled_budget_below_min_is_rejected(self):
         """SDK doc: ``budget_tokens`` must be >= 1024."""
